dsh-config-studio
English · 中文
A settings page for the part of DSH configuration the built-in pages never reach. It lists every **a
ddressable Loader entry** in the active profile, renders a form from that plugin's own `Config` sche
ma, and writes the fields you change into the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` — through `ctx.configEdit
or`, the same writer DSH's own settings use, but without the `volatile`-only restriction.
The page appears in **Settings → Plugin configuration** (设置 → 插件配置) and follows the Harness language
n **Settings → Plugin configuration** (设置 → 插件配置) and follows the Harness language (English / 简体中文).
## Why this exists
DSH's built-in settings forms write through `settings.mutate`, which only accepts fields a plugin de
clared with `.volatile()`; writing anything else throws `Config field "<path>" is not volatile`. Eve
rything else is expected to be edited by hand in YAML.
That restriction is reasonable for live-reloadable preferences, but it leaves most of a real profile
without a UI: plugin lists, timeouts, feature switches, provider tables, and the rest. This plugin
takes the other road — the complete raw config — and lets the Host validate and apply it exactly as
oad — the complete raw config — and lets the Host validate and apply it exactly as the Loader would.
## Features
- **Browse** — every entry `configEditor.entries()` returns, with package name, field count, overrid
e badge, and current status. Search by id or package; switch between *editable only* (default) and *
all*; group by **function** (models, agents, tools, web, accounts, runtime, sessions, interface, pla
tform, other) or by **origin** (built-in / third-party); collapse sections; the browsing state survi

ves opening an entry and coming back.
- **Edit** — one field per top-level config key: text, number,
switch, select for enums, and a JSON editor for objects and arrays. Each row shows the value in eff
ect, whether it comes from the profile patch, and a one-click **Reset** back to the inherited value.
- **Review, then save** — a patch-shaped diff of what will be written, a revision check that refuse
s to overwrite a concurrent edit, and a result line that says whether the override was applied or re

moved.
- **Read-only by design** — credentials, `!!js` expressions, unsupported schema shapes, and o

versized entries are never writable here (table below).
- **Bilingual** — English and Simplified Chi
nese, following the Harness language, including the nav label, every section, and error messages.
## Install
Published on npm as `dsh-config-studio`, and also a plain `dsh.bundle` bundle with **no dependencies
and no build step**. Every source below installs the same code — pick the one that matches your hos
nd no build step**. Every source below installs the same code — pick the one that matches your host.

### Requirements

| DSH | `0.2.1-rc.5` or newer (tested on `0.2.1-rc.5` and `0.2.2-rc.1`) |
| Services | `ctx.configEd

itor` and `ctx.connection.fetch` — both ship with the Web composition |
| Node | 20+ |
| Browser | a
ny current Web GUI; the section is a normal client plugin |
The package deliberately declares no DSH version range: it is plain JavaScript with no host imports,
so it keeps installing on newer hosts instead of being gated out by a prerelease peer range.
### What the badges mean
| Badge | Meaning |

| **Overridden** (entry) | The profile patch has a `config:` record for this entry |
| **Overridden*

* (field) | This key is written in that record, so the value comes from the profile layer |
| **Read

-only** | See the table below; the field is shown for context but will not be written |
| **Third-pa
rty** | The package is not under the `@deepseek-ai/` scope |
## How it works
Two halves, both in this repository:
- **Host** (`index.js`) — three `POST` endpoints registered through `ctx.connection.fetch`, so the `
/api` fence, Host/Origin checks, and cookie authentication apply before dispatch. It imports nothing
outside Node built-ins: the form shape is read from the live `schemastery` schema the Loader alread
Node built-ins: the form shape is read from the live `schemastery` schema the Loader already holds.
| Endpoint | Body | Answers |

| `/api/config-studio/list` | `{}` | entries, status, field counts, category, origin |
| `/api/confi

g-studio/read` | `{ id }` | revision, fields, values, read-only reason |
| `/api/config-studio/write
` | `{ id, expectedRevision, changes }` | `{ ok, revision }` or `{ ok: false, error }` |
- **Client** (`client.js`) — a `settings.section` registration written in the module-loader format,
with no Harness client package imports. Controls are the plugin's own, styled with theme tokens.
Writes are validated twice: once against the plugin's schema in the request, and again inside `confi
gEditor.edit()`, which holds the profile lock, preserves comments and `!!js`, writes atomically, rel
oads the entry, and rolls the file back if the reload fails. `revision` is a hash of the entry's inh
erited layer, profile override, and raw config, so a stale form is refused instead of silently overw
layer, profile override, and raw config, so a stale form is refused instead of silently overwriting.
## Security
- Only the active profile's `cordis.patch.yml` is ever written. Home patches, command-line overlays,

and bundle layers are read but never modified.
- Only entries returned by `configEditor.entries()`

are addressable; everything else is invisible to this page.
- Secrets are never sent to the browser,

and schema error messages are scrubbed of credential text before they leave the Host.
- Logs carry

entry ids and field keys only — never configuration values.
- The browser cannot pick a different wr
ite target: the Host rebuilds the candidate config from its own copy and re-validates it.
